segments: 438 [439] and without ... {OCR?}, and he went out and the governor (Shihnah) of Nisibis met him,
and he broke him and scattered those who were with him.
And he, Ibn al-Mashtub, fled with a few men,
and he crossed into the territory of Sinjar.
And Farrukh Shah, son of Zangi, son of Mawdud, son of Zangi, heard [of this],
and he sent an army and captured him,
and brought him to him while bound.
And because that Farrukh Shah, the lord of Sinjar, was on the side of al-Ashraf,
Ibn al-Mashtub deceived him,
and made him an enemy of al-Ashraf.
And he promised with oaths
to fight until he removed Mosul from the hands of Badr al-Din,
and it would become his.
Then the lord of Sinjar released Ibn al-Mashtub,
and gave him a force of horsemen,
and he came and plundered the territory of Beth Arabaye.
And Badr al-Din heard [of it] and sent troops,
and Ibn al-Mashtub was defeated by them.
And he fled and went up to the fortress of Tal'afar,
because it belonged to the lord of Sinjar.
And when Badr al-Din heard,
he went out in person and went and fought against the fortress of Tal'afar until he captured it.
And he bound Ibn al-Mashtub and sent him to Malik al-Ashraf,
and he was imprisoned in Harran until he died.
Then Malik al-Ashraf gave Hani and Jabaljur to the lord of Amid,
and promised that he would also take the city of Dara and give it to him.
And thus, when he separated him from the lord of Mardin,
he gathered strength and came to Dunaysir,
and took control over the entire territory of Mardin.
And he shut up the lord of Mardin in the fortress,
and cut off provisions from him.
Then the lord of Amid came to al-Ashraf,
and mediated between them and made peace,
with the lord of Mardin giving Resh'ayna and thirty thousand dinars to al-Ashraf,
and Mu'azzar from the territory of Shabakhtan to the lord of Amid.
And al-Ashraf set out against Nisibis.
And the lord of Sinjar became afraid of him,
and sent an envoy to him while he was on the way,
and surrendered Sinjar to al-Ashraf.
And he took for himself Callinicus (al-Raqqah) in exchange for it,
and he went out and departed for it with his brothers, his household, and all his possessions.
And when al-Ashraf had taken Sinjar,
he began sending his forces ahead of him to Mosul,
in order to come and cross over to Erbil.
And every day a large troop of horsemen would arrive,
and he arrived after all of them at Mosul on Tuesday, the nineteenth
of the fifth month of this year.
